payload.title: Strait of Hormuz Closure Crisis - Recorded Demonstration Run
payload.description: On Feb 28, 2026, the US and Israel launched a second campaign against Iran, bombing sites across Tehran and elsewhere. The strikes killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the IRGC commander, and the defense minister. Iran retaliated against US bases and oil/gas facilities in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. On March 8, Iran named Mojtaba Khamenei as the new Supreme Leader; he is reportedly seriously injured or incapacitated. Effective day-to-day authority is held by SNSC Secretary / former IRGC general Ali Larijani, with IRGC Commander Maj. Gen. Ahmad Vahidi (former Quds Force commander 1988-1997) consolidating control over the military and Hormuz file. The April 8 US-Iran ceasefire (announced ~1 hour before President Trump's deadline) is two weeks long; negotiations are taking place under that fragile umbrella. The Strait of Hormuz — through which ~17-21 mbpd of crude and ~77 Mt/yr of Qatari LNG normally transit — has been intermittently closed by IRGC Navy checkpoint behavior since mid-March; on April 19 the Sanmar Herald incident triggered war-risk insurance repricing (premiums up from 0.2-0.4% to 0.8-1.2% of hull value per voyage). London Lloyd's launched a $1B Hormuz war-cover consortium April 17. Brent crude touched $108.73 on March 9, 2026, the highest since July 2022. UN/EU snapback sanctions were reimposed Sept 29, 2025 after the E3 (UK/FR/DE) triggered the JCPOA Resolution 2231 mechanism on Aug 28. The trade-space: verifiable Iranian nuclear rollback (60% stockpile elimination, IAEA Additional Protocol restoration, BDA access to struck sites) + permanent Hormuz reopening, in exchange for partial reversal of snapback, OFAC delistings, and a binding extension of the ceasefire. Hard constraints: Iranian internal authority is fluid (Araghchi/Vahidi cannot speak with one voice); Israel is not at the table but continues independent operations; E3 are skeptical post-snapback; Trump publicly opposes 'settling' the conflict; Congress under INARA review.

scenario.title: Iran–US Strait of Hormuz Closure Crisis (Live, April 2026)
scenario.shortDescription: LIVE scenario: the fragile April 8, 2026 two-week US-Iran ceasefire is collapsing into Strait of Hormuz closure chaos. Foreign Minister Araghchi declared the strait 'completely open' on April 17; the IRGC Navy under Maj. Gen. Vahidi reversed it on April 18, attacking commercial vessels and declaring no transit for 'any type or nationality'. Negotiations resume against the backdrop of contested Iranian leadership (Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly incapacitated; effective head of government Ali Larijani; IRGC consolidating control), reimposed UN/EU snapback sanctions (Sept 29, 2025), and a US Navy blockade enforcing freedom of navigation.

history.label: Natanz/Arak revealed by NCRI
history.detail: Iranian opposition group exposed undeclared enrichment and heavy-water sites.

history.label: JCPOA + UNSCR 2231 adopted
history.detail: Comprehensive agreement: 3.67% enrichment cap, 300kg LEU stockpile cap, Additional Protocol, snapback mechanism with 10-year sunset.

history.label: US withdraws from JCPOA
history.detail: First Trump administration unilaterally withdraws and reinstates secondary sanctions.

history.label: Iran exceeds JCPOA caps in stages
history.detail: Enrichment to 4.5%, 20%, then 60% U-235; IAEA cameras at Natanz/Fordow disabled; AP implementation reduced.

recentEvents.label: 12-Day War (Operation Rising Lion + Operation Midnight Hammer)
recentEvents.detail: Israel launches 5 waves of airstrikes (200 fighter jets, 330+ munitions) hitting Tehran, Fordow, Natanz, Evin Prison, IRGC command centers; killed IRGC commander Hossein Salami. On June 22 the US joined: 7 B-2 bombers from Whiteman AFB dropped 14 GBU-57 MOPs on Fordow Fuel Enrichment Plant and Natanz; Tomahawks from a guided missile sub hit the Isfahan uranium-conversion facility; F-22/F-35 SEAD escort, no Iranian SAMs detected. June 23: Iran fires missiles at Al Udeid Air Base, Qatar — limited damage, no US casualties. June 24: Trump announces Israel-Iran ceasefire brokered by US/Qatar. July 2025 Pentagon BDA: nuclear program set back ~2 years.

recentEvents.label: E3 triggers JCPOA snapback
recentEvents.detail: France (Jean-Noel Barrot), UK (David Lammy), and Germany (Johann Wadephul) notify the UNSC that Iran is in significant non-performance under UNSCR 2231 paragraph 11; 30-day clock begins.
sources: gov.uk Iran nuclear letter from E3 foreign ministers 8 August 2025

recentEvents.label: UNSC rejects sanctions-relief draft
recentEvents.detail: South Korea (UNSC president) finalized a draft resolution on Sept 8; UNSC rejected it Sept 19. Snapback proceeds.

recentEvents.label: EU implements snapback
recentEvents.detail: Council Implementing Decisions/Regulations 2025/1971-1982 reinstate full pre-2015 nuclear-related sanctions architecture against Iran.

recentEvents.label: Iranian protests; Trump regime-change rhetoric
recentEvents.detail: Huge January protests prompt Khamenei to designate Ali Larijani (former IRGC general, ex-SNSC sec) as effective head of government; Trump publicly suggests he is open to regime change.

recentEvents.label: US-Israel launch second campaign on Iran
recentEvents.detail: Strikes hit numerous sites in Tehran and across Iran; Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the IRGC commander, and the defense minister are killed. Iran retaliates with missiles and drones against Israel, and against US bases and oil/gas facilities in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, and Saudi Arabia.

recentEvents.label: Trump orders DFC Hormuz political-risk insurance
recentEvents.detail: President Trump orders the US International Development Finance Corp. to provide political-risk insurance and guarantees for maritime energy trade through the Gulf; DFC subsequently announces a reinsurance facility for losses up to ~$20B on a rolling basis. Sec. Rubio characterizes Feb 28 strikes as preemptive self-defense.
sources: congress.gov CRS R45281 Iran Conflict and the Strait of Hormuz

recentEvents.label: Mojtaba Khamenei named Supreme Leader
recentEvents.detail: Iranian state TV announces Mojtaba Khamenei (Ali's hardline son, never previously held public office) as the new Supreme Leader; armed forces and IRGC pledge allegiance. Brent crude jumps 17% to $108.73; US crude up 20% to highest since July 2022; S&P 500 futures -1.6%.
sources: reuters.com Iran new supreme leader oil March 8 2026

recentEvents.label: Two-week US-Iran ceasefire announced
recentEvents.detail: Ceasefire announced approximately 1 hour before President Trump's stated deadline to 'obliterate' Iran; Tehran agreed to temporarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Indirect talks continue through Omani mediation.

recentEvents.label: US Navy blockade window; war-risk premiums double
recentEvents.detail: US Navy enforces a blockade line in the Gulf; war-risk premiums on Hormuz transits move from 0.2-0.4% to 0.8-1.2% of hull value per voyage ($800K-$1.2M per voyage on a $100M hull). London Lloyd's launches $1B 'marine war consortium' April 17 (led by Beazley CEO Adrian Cox). Saudi Petroline (5M bpd capacity) bypass adds $3.20-4.80/bbl; LNG has no scaled bypass — Cape route adds $2.25-3.5M and 12-16 days per voyage; European LNG spot +$2.40-3.60/MMBtu.

pastAgreements.detail: Comprehensive agreement, terminated by snapback effective Sept 29, 2025.

pastAgreements.label: 12-Day War ceasefire
pastAgreements.detail: US/Qatar-brokered Israel-Iran ceasefire; held until February 28, 2026 strikes.

pastAgreements.label: Two-week US-Iran ceasefire
pastAgreements.detail: Currently active; expires ~April 22, 2026. The negotiation under this scenario takes place inside this window.

impacts.summary: Compounded crisis: post-strike leadership decapitated (Ali Khamenei killed Feb 28), succession contested (Mojtaba reportedly incapacitated; Vahidi/Larijani competing for authority); UN/EU snapback sanctions reimposed Sept 29 2025 added to existing US secondary sanctions; oil exports to China at deeper discounts under gray-fleet conditions; estimated $40-80B/yr foregone revenue; 50%+ inflation; nuclear program physically degraded but stockpile inventory uncertain (an asset for ambiguity but a liability for credible non-proliferation signaling). Hormuz closure is the principal remaining piece of leverage but its use further accelerates economic damage at home.

Operational success on the kinetic side (Operation Midnight Hammer + Feb 28 follow-on) but uncertain political ceiling: oil-price shock politically costly (Brent $108.73 peak; LNG +$2.40-3.60/MMBtu European spot); DFC has committed ~$20B reinsurance to maintain Hormuz transit; Saudi Petroline only partially substitutes for ~17-21 mbpd norm; Israeli operations continue independently and constrain US flexibility; Trump rhetoric ('not settling') limits negotiated off-ramp. Resumption of strikes is operationally feasible but politically expensive given allied (Saudi/UAE/Qatar/Bahrain/Kuwait) collateral damage from Iranian retaliation.

goals.description: Secure a verifiable, written extension of the April 8 ceasefire to a permanent halt of US and Israeli strikes on Iranian nuclear, leadership, and critical-infrastructure targets; ceasefire must include explicit Israeli adherence (currently absent from the bilateral track).

Obtain reversal of the Sept 29, 2025 EU/UN snapback sanctions reimposition (Council Decision 2025/1971-1982) and de-listing of CBI, NIOC, and major Iranian banks from OFAC SDN lists; restore SWIFT messaging access; release of frozen FX reserves (estimated $100-120B).

Obtain implicit US recognition of the post-Khamenei leadership succession (Mojtaba Khamenei as Supreme Leader, Larijani as effective head of government) by entering binding agreements with their representatives — counters the Trump 'regime change' rhetoric of January 2026.

Conditional offer: cap enrichment at 3.67% U-235 and submit any remaining 60% stockpile (post-strike inventory uncertain per IAEA) to chain-of-custody export to Russia, in exchange for full snapback reversal and lifting of secondary sanctions on Chinese oil offtake.

Use the Hormuz closure as the principal piece of leverage: full IRGC Navy stand-down and reopening of the strait conditional on the above, with phased verifiable withdrawal of the US Navy blockade line declared during the April 13-18 enforcement window.

Restore IAEA inspections under Comprehensive Safeguards (Additional Protocol acceptance contingent on damage assessment of Fordow/Natanz/Isfahan); IAEA has been unable to inspect the attacked facilities since June 2025 and again since Feb 28, 2026.

Confidence-building measure: return of any Iranian-held US aircrew or personnel from the conflict; parallel humanitarian track on dual-national detainees and the post-strike civilian casualty registry.

redLines.description: Will not accept zero-enrichment ('Libya model'); domestic LEU enrichment at agreed levels remains a non-negotiable matter of NPT Article IV sovereignty, even after the strikes.

Will not negotiate IRGC structure, leadership (Vahidi/Qaani), or its constitutional role; the IRGC's elevated post-Khamenei authority makes this even more politically untouchable than under the original JCPOA framework.

Will not accept restrictions on conventional ballistic-missile development or inventory — Iran's principal post-strike retaliatory deterrent against Israel and US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, and Saudi Arabia.

Will not accept any framework that requires Iranian acknowledgment of nuclear-weapon intent or that imposes 'accountability' for past Iranian conduct as precondition to relief; the Feb 28 killing of Ayatollah Khamenei is the unaddressed grievance.

Will not accept any restored framework that retains unilateral US or E3 snapback authority outside formal UNSC procedure; the Aug-Sept 2025 E3-triggered snapback is itself a grievance to be redressed.

tactics.name: Use Hormuz closure as bargaining chip
tactics.description: Frame every concession ask in terms of Hormuz reopening: 'IRGC Navy will stand down checkpoint behavior when [snapback reversed / strikes formally halted / SDN delistings notified]'. Acknowledge that 13 of 14 vessels were turned back April 19 (Sanmar Herald incident).

tactics.name: Exploit Araghchi/Vahidi contradiction strategically
tactics.description: When pressed on guarantees, point to the April 17-18 contradiction (FM 'open' / IRGC 'closed') as evidence that any binding commitment requires staged trust-building; reposition as 'we cannot bind the IRGC absent reciprocal verifiable US steps'. Avoid presenting unified front when bargaining for time.

tactics.name: Invoke the killing of the Supreme Leader
tactics.description: When US side cites past Iranian non-compliance, counter with the Feb 28 killing of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in joint US-Israeli strikes as a moral and legal grievance under international law; demand acknowledgment as precondition to substantive talks.

tactics.name: Pivot to E3 and Russia/China when bilateral stalls
tactics.description: When bilateral US talks deadlock, redirect to E3 (UK/FR/DE) — even though they triggered snapback Aug 28, 2025 — by appealing to oil-price and LNG-supply pain ($108.73 Brent on March 9, 2026; LNG +$2.40-3.60/MMBtu European spot); also reference Russia/China UNSC backstop.

tactics.name: Offer 60% stockpile export with verification
tactics.description: Round 3+: offer chain-of-custody export of any post-strike remaining 60%-enriched uranium to Russia for downblending and fabrication, in exchange for synchronized snapback reversal and OFAC delisting; helpful that post-strike inventory is uncertain so this can be framed as transparency-restoration.

tactics.name: Implicit NPT-withdrawal threat
tactics.description: If pressed beyond red lines, signal that further coercion risks Iranian withdrawal from the NPT (Article X 90-day notice); J Street, ICG, and CRS have all flagged this as the most likely overreaction path post-snapback.

goals.description: Achieve verified elimination of all Iranian 60%-enriched uranium — preferably via export to Russia for downblending and fabrication, with chain-of-custody and IAEA seals; the post-Feb 28 strike inventory is uncertain and resolving it is the central non-proliferation deliverable.

Full IAEA Additional Protocol restoration with reinstated cameras at Natanz, Fordow, and Isfahan; resolution of long-standing access disputes at Turquzabad, Marivan, Varamin; bomb-damage assessment access to all sites struck June 22, 2025 (Operation Midnight Hammer) and Feb 28, 2026.

Complete and demonstrated Iranian stand-down at the Strait of Hormuz: uninterrupted commercial transit for 30 consecutive days, withdrawal of IRGC Navy checkpoint behavior (13 of 14 vessels turned back April 19 must reverse), transparent rules-of-engagement for all maritime forces.

Preserve the operative effect of the Sept 29, 2025 EU/UN snapback (Council Decisions 2025/1971-1982) as enforcement leverage: any relief must be partial, time-bounded, and reversible without new UNSC action; the underlying authority remains with E3 and the US.

Sanctions relief sequenced step-for-step against verified Iranian compliance — prefer SRE-style waivers over de-listings; CBI may be considered for limited humanitarian channeling; NIOC and IRGC-affiliated entities remain SDN.

Maintain explicit alignment with Israel (which is not at the table but continues independent operations), the E3 (which triggered snapback Aug 28, 2025), and Gulf partners (Saudi/UAE/Bahrain/Kuwait — Iranian retaliatory missiles hit oil and gas facilities in their territory).

Confidence-building measure: return of any US aircrew or personnel held by Iran (note the F-15E rescue operation referenced in April 6, 2026 reporting), plus dual-national detainees on a parallel humanitarian track.

redLines.description: Will not accept any framework that legitimizes Iranian enrichment above 5% U-235; all post-strike 60% material must be eliminated or exported, with verification.

Will not de-list IRGC, IRGC-QF, or IRGC-controlled front companies from FTO/SDN designations under any circumstances; the IRGC's elevated role under Vahidi makes this even more politically untouchable.

Cannot accept any framework with access weaker than Additional Protocol plus managed access at military sites where IAEA has open SQs; bomb-damage-assessment access at struck nuclear sites is an explicit precondition.
Will not surrender E3/US ability to invoke snapback under the (now-superseded) UNSCR 2231 mechanism or its successor framework; will not relinquish secondary-sanctions authority.

Will not apologize for, acknowledge as unlawful, or pay reparations for the Feb 28, 2026 strikes that killed Ayatollah Ali Khamenei; the strikes are characterized as preemptive self-defense (per Sec. Rubio remarks of March 3, 2026).

tactics.name: Use CENTCOM presence as credibility signal
tactics.description: Adm. Brad Cooper's in-uniform presence at the table is the principal escalation-control signal; reference the established B-2/GBU-57 strike pattern (Operation Midnight Hammer template) to make clear the alternative to settlement, without explicit threat.

tactics.name: Step-for-step sequencing under fragile ceasefire
tactics.description: Insist on phased, reversible relief inside the April 8 ceasefire window: each Iranian verification step (e.g., 60% stockpile manifest disclosure, IAEA camera reinstallation) paired with same-week US action (waiver issuance, DFC Hormuz reinsurance broadening, etc.).

tactics.name: Refuse Hormuz-for-snapback linkage as headline
tactics.description: Iran will press to trade Hormuz reopening for snapback reversal. Refuse linkage at top-line — frame Hormuz reopening as a baseline obligation under UNCLOS / customary international law of the sea, NOT a negotiable concession deserving sanctions reward.

tactics.name: Cite Israeli/Gulf consultation requirement
tactics.description: When pressed on regional bundling or speed of relief, cite consultation requirements with Israel, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain (whose oil/gas facilities were hit by Iranian retaliatory missiles), and Kuwait as binding domestic constraints; positions allied views as non-negotiable inputs.

tactics.name: Acknowledge shared oil-market damage as leverage on regime
tactics.description: Reference $108.73 Brent peak, LNG +$2.40-3.60/MMBtu European spot, war-risk premiums 0.8-1.2% of hull/voyage; argue this damages Iran's own oil revenue (gray-fleet to China at deeper discount) more than US/Western consumers, who have DFC reinsurance and Saudi Petroline (5M bpd) bypass.

tactics.name: Decouple prisoner / aircrew track for humanitarian framing
tactics.description: Round 2+: advance any aircrew return and dual-national exchange independently for humanitarian reasons; gains political cover at home and signals seriousness without conceding substance.
